messages.subject: Comparing lavaan and Mplus
parts:
I would want to move to lavaan for many of my SEM analyses. But differences in the two programs' estimations may differ sufficiently, resulting in different conclusions for model fit. For each model parameter, differences were minor, but apparently the aggregated effects of these deviations may to lead different conclusions on whether the model  is above the threshold for overall fit. 

I'm not saying that Mplus is correct, by no means. But Mplus is to many people the gold standard in latent variable modelling, and lavaan is certainly inspired by Mplus. Shouldn't results be more similar? Since they are not, how do I justify using lavaan over Mplus and use a model that Mplus would reject (if my cutoff for RMSEA is .05)?

Christopher

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Comparing lavaan and Mplus
parts:
On 03/13/2018 12:25 AM, Christopher Bratt wrote:
> I'm not saying that Mplus is correct, by no means. But Mplus is to many
> people the gold standard in latent variable modelling, and lavaan is
> certainly inspired by Mplus. Shouldn't results be more similar? Since
> they are not, how do I justify using lavaan over Mplus and use a model
> that Mplus would reject (if my cutoff for RMSEA is .05)?

This would be my argument: I can explain to you how we got to 4486.959.
I can show you the formulas, and more importantly, the source code. You
can check it line by line. Many people have done so.

The question you should ask is: can the Mplus people explain how they
got 5442.385? Of course they can, but I don't think they will tell you.
There are no formulas (believe me, I looked hard).

For your particular example, first check the sample statistics
(thresholds, correlations). If they are already different, everything
else will be different. Then check the parameter estimates. Rerun the
model with complete data (listwise = on), to see if the way both
programs handle missing data (in the categorical case!) has anything to
do with it. Next, change the estimator to WLS, so we can check if we are
using the same weight matrix, and so on.

Yes, ideally, the mimic="Mplus" should be spot on. Often it is.
Sometimes it fails to mimic the Mplus numbers. That is because I have no
clue how they are computed. I already spent way too much effort on this
mimic="Mplus" feature. It is time to focus on lavaan, not Mplus.

Yves.

messages.author: 572119bb37de95d7
messages.subject: Re: Comparing lavaan and Mplus
parts:
Yes Yves, I think this is a very good answer. You, and thus the researcher, can document how the package arrived at its conclusions. Mplus cannot. Whom do we trust? Those documenting their computations or those who don't?
